sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
UChicago bachelor completed before entry satisfies the US bachelor-level qualification; selection remains
competitive. Mathematics admits full-time fall PhD students only, not terminal master’s applicants or a
primarily teaching-oriented doctorate. F-1 is not an academic exclusion. [s1] [s2] [s5]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose Mathematics PhD; prepare transcripts, CV, two statements and three academic referees. Calculate GPA
on the requested 4.0 scale. Check English exemption under Additional Academic Information. Enter
recommenders early; math advises at least one month’s notice and reminder a week before deadline. [s2] [s4]
[s5] [s13]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Faculty contact is encouraged as a short introduction and notice of application, not a prerequisite supervisor
agreement. Indicate relevant people in the application; newer faculty may be absent from the menu and can
be written in. Academic questions: math-phd-program@duke.edu; application processing: Graduate School. [s4]
[s1]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Request letters early, upload required documents and monitor status. Reapplicants file a new application. Do
not work on multiple Duke applications simultaneously in the same browser because data may be overwritten.
Updated CV or scores can be appended; transcript corrections should be emailed as PDF with identifying
information. Originals remain on record. [s5] [s11]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Department and central deadline explicitly cover Fall 2027; funding amounts currently found cover 2026-27.
[s1] [s3] [s16]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [2027 confirmed]
TOEFL, IELTS or DET unless exempt. Generally TOEFL 90 (tests before 21 January 2026) or 5 (new scale), IELTS
7, DET 125 with subscores. For Fall 2027, tests must be dated on/after 1 August 2024. TOEFL Home Edition
accepted; Essentials and IELTS Indicator not accepted. Official agency delivery; ETS code 5156. [s13]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
UChicago should qualify if at least two years of full-time study with English as the sole instruction language are
completed by program start. Record the exemption in Additional Academic Information; Duke does not
review/confirm waiver eligibility until an admission offer. Nonnative international admittees still take
placement testing and may need English-language courses. [s13]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [2027 confirmed]
Optional for Fall 2027; scores may be submitted but neither GRE is required. This is not a not-considered
policy. [s1]

Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload unofficial transcripts from every institution where a degree is earned/expected, a semester or more was
attended, at least 12 credits were earned, or courses in the intended field were taken. Study-abroad transcript
may be unnecessary if all credits appear on the home transcript. Include course/grade/year details,
institutional grading scale and original plus professional English translation when necessary. No
student-system screenshots. Remove SSN except final four digits. Transcript-specific rule: unlocked PDF, at
most 1.5 MB, preview before submitting. Official records are requested after acceptance. Missing records
require a documented explanation and admissions contact. [s12]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three, preferably professors in the major or research supervisors. Additional letters are strongly discouraged
unless the program requests them. [s9]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
Initial University Scholars fellowship is department-nominated, with no direct applicant application identified.
No additional applicant reference or different referee questionnaire was established for standard math support.
External awards may differ. [s20] [s15]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Adding recommender contact details triggers an email soon afterward, before final submission if desired. Use
professional email where available; senders should check spam for grad-admissions@duke.edu. Recommender
completes relationship questions and uploads a letter. [s9] [s10]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Invitations can be sent before submission; applicant may submit before all letters/scores arrive. Deadlines still
apply. [s10]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Post-submission portal tracks receipt and completeness. Incomplete applications may not be reviewed. [s11]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
After final submission, contact admissions to replace an unavailable recommender. Interfolio is permitted using
its specific recommender email. Reapplication requires new requests; a referee may resubmit an older letter if
still relevant. No automatic carry-forward or public rule for replacing a submitted letter was verified. [s10]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required uploaded resume/CV; include education, academic/professional accomplishments, experience, and
optionally research/publications/skills. No CV-specific length, font or margin rule published. General upload
instructions specify PDF. Post-submission CV additions append rather than replace. [s8] [s5]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required uploaded statement, 1-2 pages, single-spaced; mathematics recommends under two pages. Prompt
paraphrase: academic preparation and work, research interests and goals, strengths/weaknesses, significant
research and impact, why Duke and relevant faculty; explain a transition from another field if applicable.
Upload under Required Supplemental Uploads. No public font/margin rule identified. [s6] [s2]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Required Life Experiences Statement, at most one single-spaced page, uploaded under Additional Experiences.
Prompt paraphrase: formative life experiences shaping personal/professional identity, preparation for graduate
work, perspectives brought to Duke and contribution to its academic community. The guidance discusses
resilience and inclusive engagement; no public font/margin rule identified. [s7]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Include research interests and faculty/program fit in the SOP. A separate research-interest statement is not
listed; no separate prompt/limit/upload rule established. [s6] [s2]
Research proposal [Unresolved]
No separate admission research proposal listed. Enrolled math students in years 1-2 later submit a short
summer-research-plan proposal for guaranteed summer fellowship support; that is not a prospective applicant
essay. Admission-portal extras remain unverified. [s2] [s18]

Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
2027-28 math cash stipend not published in reviewed sources. The 2026-27 recommended university schedule
is not a math offer: first-year 10-month August-May stipend USD 32,831.40; first-year full 13-month
August-August total USD 43,775.16; continuing 12-month August-July total USD 43,775.16. Three-month
summer line is USD 10,943.79; minor table rounding differences must not be treated as extra money. Tuition,
mandatory fees, and health/dental coverage are separate from cash support. [s16] [s17]
Years of support [Standing rule]
All math admits are offered five years of funding. University standard covers stipend, tuition and mandatory
fees for five years, health/dental insurance for six. Sixth-year tuition/mandatory-fee backstop can apply after
unsuccessful efforts to secure other funding; no universal sixth-year stipend guarantee. [s15] [s17]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
The department’s promise covers all admitted students; inference: admitted international PhDs are included.
Citizenship-specific fellowships must be checked separately. Dean’s Graduate Fellowship is domestic-only and
should not be budgeted for an F-1 applicant. [s15] [s21]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Full-time enrollment, good standing and satisfactory progress; five consecutive years standard support.
Research/teaching appointments and applicable assistantship obligations depend on offer. Math summer years
1-2: guaranteed research fellowship, March notification and short proposal. Years 3-5: seek other sources;
Trinity summer backstop requires at least one other funding application. [s18] [s19]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No separate initial math funding application listed. Later summer proposal/backstop processes apply as
described under funding conditions. University Scholars is departmental nomination, not direct application.
[s15] [s18] [s20]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Department/adviser research support, external fellowships, summer awards and University Scholars fellowship
may supplement the funding route. Award eligibility varies; the University Scholars public overview does not

establish a citizenship restriction, while the Dean’s fellowship explicitly restricts to domestic applicants. [s18]
[s20] [s21]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 105 nonrefundable, paid by application deadline; fee page lists Visa, Discover and MasterCard. [s14]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Central waivers require US citizenship/permanent residence plus qualifying financial need, military status or a
listed participation program; this does not ordinarily cover an F-1 international applicant. Requests use the
application, limited first-come funds. Although central instructions mention possible program codes,
Mathematics explicitly says it has no waivers. Do not rely on another Duke department’s exceptions. [s14] [s1]

Duke University
United States · Mathematics PhD
2026 US News roster/rank verified separately
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Mathematics explicitly has no application-fee waivers; central domestic eligibility does not ordinarily cover
F-1 applicants.
• English exemption is not formally reviewed until admission.
• First-year recommended funding is quoted on a 13-month basis; 2027-28 math-specific stipend remains
unverified.
• Current faculty research match does not guarantee supervision; Hain is emeritus and Plesser is secondary in
mathematics.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
UChicago bachelor completed before entry satisfies the US bachelor-level qualification; selection remains
competitive. Mathematics admits full-time fall PhD students only, not terminal master’s applicants or a
primarily teaching-oriented doctorate. F-1 is not an academic exclusion. [s1] [s2] [s5]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose Mathematics PhD; prepare transcripts, CV, two statements and three academic referees. Calculate GPA
on the requested 4.0 scale. Check English exemption under Additional Academic Information. Enter
recommenders early; math advises at least one month’s notice and reminder a week before deadline. [s2] [s4]
[s5] [s13]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Faculty contact is encouraged as a short introduction and notice of application, not a prerequisite supervisor
agreement. Indicate relevant people in the application; newer faculty may be absent from the menu and can
be written in. Academic questions: math-phd-program@duke.edu; application processing: Graduate School. [s4]
[s1]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Request letters early, upload required documents and monitor status. Reapplicants file a new application. Do
not work on multiple Duke applications simultaneously in the same browser because data may be overwritten.
Updated CV or scores can be appended; transcript corrections should be emailed as PDF with identifying
information. Originals remain on record. [s5] [s11]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Department and central deadline explicitly cover Fall 2027; funding amounts currently found cover 2026-27.
[s1] [s3] [s16]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application; Supporting documents [2027 confirmed]
15 December 2026, 11:59:59 p.m. EST, for Fall 2027. All required materials should be complete; central
deadlines control if a departmental page differs. [s3]

Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
Submit the complete admission application by 15 December 2026. All math admits receive the standard
funding offer; no separate initial departmental aid deadline is listed. Named external awards have separate
rules. [s1] [s15]
Reference receipt [Standing rule]
Letters should arrive by the application deadline, 15 December 2026. Late letters are forwarded, but timely
review is not assured. There is no published separate later guaranteed reference deadline. [s3] [s10]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Any required official scores should reach Duke by the application deadline. Late scores may be matched
without guaranteed consideration. Matching commonly takes 2-3 business days after submission; allow agency
processing time. [s3] [s10]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
Standing FAQ gives fall admittees until April 15 or 15 days after receipt of the admission letter, whichever is
later. Confirm the exact date and any interim check-in in the 2027 offer. [s10]
English and GRE
English requirement [2027 confirmed]
TOEFL, IELTS or DET unless exempt. Generally TOEFL 90 (tests before 21 January 2026) or 5 (new scale), IELTS
7, DET 125 with subscores. For Fall 2027, tests must be dated on/after 1 August 2024. TOEFL Home Edition
accepted; Essentials and IELTS Indicator not accepted. Official agency delivery; ETS code 5156. [s13]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
UChicago should qualify if at least two years of full-time study with English as the sole instruction language are
completed by program start. Record the exemption in Additional Academic Information; Duke does not
review/confirm waiver eligibility until an admission offer. Nonnative international admittees still take
placement testing and may need English-language courses. [s13]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [2027 confirmed]
Optional for Fall 2027; scores may be submitted but neither GRE is required. This is not a not-considered
policy. [s1]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload unofficial transcripts from every institution where a degree is earned/expected, a semester or more was
attended, at least 12 credits were earned, or courses in the intended field were taken. Study-abroad transcript
may be unnecessary if all credits appear on the home transcript. Include course/grade/year details,
institutional grading scale and original plus professional English translation when necessary. No
student-system screenshots. Remove SSN except final four digits. Transcript-specific rule: unlocked PDF, at
most 1.5 MB, preview before submitting. Official records are requested after acceptance. Missing records
require a documented explanation and admissions contact. [s12]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Unresolved]
A separate mathematics course list or course-description attachment was not found in the public
math/program/central checklist. Transcript is required. Any portal-only course-list prompt, limit or file rule
remains unverified; do not infer permission for an extra upload. [s1] [s2] [s5]

Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three, preferably professors in the major or research supervisors. Additional letters are strongly discouraged
unless the program requests them. [s9]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
Initial University Scholars fellowship is department-nominated, with no direct applicant application identified.
No additional applicant reference or different referee questionnaire was established for standard math support.
External awards may differ. [s20] [s15]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Adding recommender contact details triggers an email soon afterward, before final submission if desired. Use
professional email where available; senders should check spam for grad-admissions@duke.edu. Recommender
completes relationship questions and uploads a letter. [s9] [s10]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Invitations can be sent before submission; applicant may submit before all letters/scores arrive. Deadlines still
apply. [s10]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Post-submission portal tracks receipt and completeness. Incomplete applications may not be reviewed. [s11]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
After final submission, contact admissions to replace an unavailable recommender. Interfolio is permitted using
its specific recommender email. Reapplication requires new requests; a referee may resubmit an older letter if
still relevant. No automatic carry-forward or public rule for replacing a submitted letter was verified. [s10]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required uploaded resume/CV; include education, academic/professional accomplishments, experience, and
optionally research/publications/skills. No CV-specific length, font or margin rule published. General upload
instructions specify PDF. Post-submission CV additions append rather than replace. [s8] [s5]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required uploaded statement, 1-2 pages, single-spaced; mathematics recommends under two pages. Prompt
paraphrase: academic preparation and work, research interests and goals, strengths/weaknesses, significant
research and impact, why Duke and relevant faculty; explain a transition from another field if applicable.
Upload under Required Supplemental Uploads. No public font/margin rule identified. [s6] [s2]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Required Life Experiences Statement, at most one single-spaced page, uploaded under Additional Experiences.
Prompt paraphrase: formative life experiences shaping personal/professional identity, preparation for graduate
work, perspectives brought to Duke and contribution to its academic community. The guidance discusses
resilience and inclusive engagement; no public font/margin rule identified. [s7]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Include research interests and faculty/program fit in the SOP. A separate research-interest statement is not
listed; no separate prompt/limit/upload rule established. [s6] [s2]
Research proposal [Unresolved]
No separate admission research proposal listed. Enrolled math students in years 1-2 later submit a short
summer-research-plan proposal for guaranteed summer fellowship support; that is not a prospective applicant
essay. Admission-portal extras remain unverified. [s2] [s18]

Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
Program listing explicitly says no writing sample is required. Optional thesis/paper upload or link permission is
not established; central guidance discourages unnecessary extra material. [s2] [s5]
Publications list [Standing rule]
Publications may be included in the CV. No separate publication-list document or requirement to upload papers
was established; paper linking/upload permission is unverified. [s8]
Course-list document [Unresolved]
A separate mathematics course list or course-description attachment was not found in the public
math/program/central checklist. Transcript is required. Any portal-only course-list prompt, limit or file rule
remains unverified; do not infer permission for an extra upload. [s1] [s2] [s5]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
No separate initial standard-support essay found. University Scholars awards use department nomination.
Summer-support proposals for enrolled students have their own later process; exact limits and dates are not
supplied on the overview. [s15] [s18] [s20]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Public central checklist does not identify another mathematics-specific essay. General uploads are PDF; central
generic maximum is 75 pages/5 GB, but transcript-specific 1.5 MB rule controls. These ceilings are not
recommended essay lengths. Put name on application documents. [s5] [s12]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
2027-28 math cash stipend not published in reviewed sources. The 2026-27 recommended university schedule
is not a math offer: first-year 10-month August-May stipend USD 32,831.40; first-year full 13-month
August-August total USD 43,775.16; continuing 12-month August-July total USD 43,775.16. Three-month
summer line is USD 10,943.79; minor table rounding differences must not be treated as extra money. Tuition,
mandatory fees, and health/dental coverage are separate from cash support. [s16] [s17]
Years of support [Standing rule]
All math admits are offered five years of funding. University standard covers stipend, tuition and mandatory
fees for five years, health/dental insurance for six. Sixth-year tuition/mandatory-fee backstop can apply after
unsuccessful efforts to secure other funding; no universal sixth-year stipend guarantee. [s15] [s17]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
The department’s promise covers all admitted students; inference: admitted international PhDs are included.
Citizenship-specific fellowships must be checked separately. Dean’s Graduate Fellowship is domestic-only and
should not be budgeted for an F-1 applicant. [s15] [s21]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Full-time enrollment, good standing and satisfactory progress; five consecutive years standard support.
Research/teaching appointments and applicable assistantship obligations depend on offer. Math summer years
1-2: guaranteed research fellowship, March notification and short proposal. Years 3-5: seek other sources;
Trinity summer backstop requires at least one other funding application. [s18] [s19]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No separate initial math funding application listed. Later summer proposal/backstop processes apply as
described under funding conditions. University Scholars is departmental nomination, not direct application.
[s15] [s18] [s20]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Department/adviser research support, external fellowships, summer awards and University Scholars fellowship
may supplement the funding route. Award eligibility varies; the University Scholars public overview does not

establish a citizenship restriction, while the Dean’s fellowship explicitly restricts to domestic applicants. [s18]
[s20] [s21]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 105 nonrefundable, paid by application deadline; fee page lists Visa, Discover and MasterCard. [s14]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Central waivers require US citizenship/permanent residence plus qualifying financial need, military status or a
listed participation program; this does not ordinarily cover an F-1 international applicant. Requests use the
application, limited first-come funds. Although central instructions mention possible program codes,
